> Connor — thanks again for the walkthrough today. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we lock down the evaluation timeline:  
> 
> - We want a 6-week hands-on eval with a production-like workload (multi-region, primary US, EU failover).
> - Need clarity on how commercial terms change when we require data residency in EU and a cross-region failover SLA (we expect a higher price for residency + failover).
> - For the MAP (mutual action plan), our procurement wants milestones tied to pricing: POC start, 50% ramp (tokens/requests), and production go-live — each milestone should release committed discounts.

Thanks Ben — we can absolutely structure a MAP that ties milestone acceptance to staged discounts and to committed capacity. Drafted a short plan and term summary attached for your review (redwood-map-v2.pdf + SLA-cross-region-term-sheet.xlsx). Key points up front:  

- Evaluation cadence: 6 weeks as requested. Week 0: onboarding + test dataset load. Weeks 1–4: performance validation and scale tests. Weeks 5–6: production pilot/traffic mirroring.
- Commercial flow: we propose a three-stage commitment: Trial (no commit, discounted trial credits), Ramp (30% committed baseline usage for 3 months -> releases 10% discount), Production (12-month commit at negotiated rate -> additional 15% discount). Discounts are cumulative but gated to milestone acceptance and verified telemetry.
- Regional residency & failover premium: EU data residency is a +12% premium on base unit price; cross-region active-passive failover SLA (30s RTO across regions) is an additional +6%. We can cap the combined premium at +18% for multi-year commits.
- Failover commercial terms: We offer a materiality-based credit (pro-rated) if failover latency exceeds SLA more than 2x in a 30-day window; we do not accept liability for third-party cloud outages but we provide prioritized remediation and optional multi-zone redundancy for an extra fee.

I'll loop Marissa and Karthik for commercial/legal fine-tuning. If that high-level structure looks good, we'll convert the draft into a MAP with milestone acceptance criteria so your procurement can sign off.

Connor O'Brien

Connor / Karthik — forwarding Connor's draft and Ben's ask. A few commercial/legal notes before we return to Acme:  

- The proposed +12% residency / +6% failover premiums are reasonable starting points but we should offer a softened schedule for the Ramp milestone: for the 3-month ramp commit, suggest a reduced residency premium (+8%) to lower friction.
- For discounts tied to milestones: require telemetry + a short acceptance window (5 business days) where Acme validates throughput/latency against agreed test cases. If they miss acceptance, milestone waits but trial credits continue. This avoids premature discount release.
- Legal: limit the combined SLA credit exposure to 3 months of committed fees (cap) and ensure a force majeure carve-out for cloud provider incidents. Also add a rollback clause allowing Acme to drop residency requirement if regulatory posture changes within 90 days with 60-day notice (we want to avoid being locked into an expensive residency premium).

Karthik — can you draft a short clause list we can include in the term-sheet? Laura — can you confirm whether finance can accept the proposed cumulative discount stacking (Ramp + Production) or if we need a different incentive structure (e.g., credits vs. list price discounts)?

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa — agreed on the acceptance window and the force majeure carve-out. Drafted core term bullets below for inclusion in SLA-cross-region-term-sheet.xlsx and the MAP:  

1) Milestones & Verification:
- POC Start: onboarding complete and baseline tests executed. No commit; trial credits applied.
- Ramp Acceptance (50% expected usage for 3 continuous weeks): acceptance defined as meeting throughput >=50% of agreed baseline and 95th percentile latency within agreed tolerance over a 14-day run. Upon acceptance, the Ramp discount (10%) is applied to the baseline for the following quarter.
- Production Go-Live: 12-month commit at agreed baseline. Production discount (15%) applies after billing cycle following successful cutover.

2) Residency & Failover Premiums:
- Data residency in EU: +12% base premium; for 3-month ramp-only commitments reduce to +8% as a transitional concession.
- Cross-region failover SLA (active-passive): +6% premium. Combined premiums capped at +18% unless a bespoke network/HA architecture is requested.

3) SLA Credit & Liability:
- SLA credit limited to 3 months of committed fees per 12-month period; no consequential damages; force majeure includes cloud provider outages.

4) Rollback & Change Control:
- Acme may propose residency removal with 60-day notice; Redwood reserves the right to reprice and requires a 90-day transition window to remove data segregation controls.

Connor — I'm attaching a short legal summary to the Drive link and will convert these bullets into redlines for the term-sheet. Marissa / Laura — let me know on the incentive structure.
